## 1. FT84-Q01 — Spell Scribe applies to qualifying written ritual copying

### Selected interpretation

**Ritual Caster’s written-learning route qualifies for Spell Scribe when the learner actually works from a complete, legitimately accessible written version of the eligible ritual and records it in a real usable ritual book.**

The predicate is the actual work, not the presence or absence of another person. A tutor does not disqualify genuine copying. Conversely, writing notes while a teacher supplies otherwise missing instruction does not turn teacher-led learning into complete-source copying.

| Actual route | Required rank-one active work |
|---|---:|
| Qualifying written copying with Spell Scribe | **240 minutes** |
| Teacher-led learning without that complete written source | **480 minutes** |
| Qualifying written copying with an advisory tutor present | **240 minutes**, with any actual separate service agreement retained |

The existing **15-minute study phases**, language/notation access, complete learning and recording requirements, book, tools and actual costs remain. There is still **no random completion roll, free starting ritual, ordinary Wizard spellbook acquisition or trade XP**.

Diligent Researcher does not halve this again. Wizard Spell Scribing remains its own source-qualified class procedure; simply being a Wizard does not substitute its price and learning route for Ritual Caster.

### New narrow material-bill completion

**No universal mundane/rare split is invented for the ten-gp bill.** A material discount requires actual identified stock and categories.

Identified ordinary writing stock, ordinary ink and mundane practice supplies can receive Spell Scribe’s reduction. Rare inks and unique or specifically required components remain full quantity. Instructor/facility fees, copying rights, reusable tools and the separate book do not become mundane consumables merely by being included on an invoice.

An unitemized complete bill can still be supplied in full at its genuine price. **Unsupported material classification does not cancel the independent half-time benefit.** Missing actual materials, however, remains a real prerequisite.

The worked bill demonstrates the distinction:

| Actual fixture material | Original requirement | With Spell Scribe |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary sheets at 25 cp each | 4 sheets / 100 cp | 3 sheets / 75 cp |
| Divisible ordinary ink at 100 cp/unit | 5 units / 500 cp | 3.75 units / 375 cp |
| Rare ink at 100 cp/unit | 4 units / 400 cp | **4 units / 400 cp** |
| **Total** | **1,000 cp** | **850 cp** |

This is an itemized example, **not a universal ritual recipe**. Divisible quantities retain precision; indivisible units round upward; the aggregate purchase rounds upward to copper once.

The interruption case also preserves real losses: 25 minutes interrupted during its second phase yields **15 credited minutes and 10 lost minutes**. After a five-minute gap and 225 more active minutes, the ritual finishes with **240 credited / 250 actual / 255 elapsed minutes**. Actual wasted ink remains consumed.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}[Complete source excerpts and classification basis](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Feat335_Work_Compositions_84_Part5_Return_01/SOURCE_EXCERPTS.md)

## 2. FT84-Q02 — explicit phase completion for two named research processes

### Existing rules remain distinct

Language teaching already has its 15-minute phases. Ritual Caster expressly uses that study clock. Advanced manufacturing has its own included incorporation phase and later phases of at most eight hours.

**Those facts do not establish a universal research clock.**

### New narrow selection

For these two procedures only, where no more-specific phase rule applies:

**A.** LA-07’s ordinary, preregistered **Translate/Decipher project of at most 250 words**.  
**B.** Crafting/Harvest’s research of an **existing available formula**.

Select **completed 15-active-minute credit phases plus the exact shorter final remainder**. This is explicitly **NEW authorship for A/B**, not an assertion that teaching’s rule already controlled them.

Establish the full source requirement first: 480 minutes for A, and `60 × max(8, actual minimumResearchHours)` minutes for B. Apply the strongest genuinely applicable research-time factor once. Track the final requirement in active seconds, rounding upward only if the final exact requirement contains a fractional second.

That is **local work-ledger precision**, not a new global simulation tick or encounter cadence.

A real interruption loses unfinished phase credit, not completed phases or the historical record of actual work. Used stock, paid fees and genuine losses remain. Research phases do **not** incorporate or stabilize manufacturing ingredients.

### Useful positive and boundary cases

Both worked eight-hour research projects require **240 credited minutes** with Diligent Researcher. Their interruption/resumption examples finish at **250 actual work minutes and 255 elapsed minutes**.

The language example uses the actual one-assistant rule:

```text
d20 7 + INT 3 + PB 4 + qualified assistant 1 = 15
DC 15: success
```

Without that actual contribution, the total is **14** and the result is notes—not a fabricated translation. The assistant must perform the adjusted required work; actual attendance and fees are recorded.

The formula example uses the actual recipe121 DC:

```text
d20 5 + INT 3 + PB 3 = 11
DC 8: success
```

It yields the supported formula transcription, **not an enchanted item or trade XP**. Its manufacturing crystals, rib and reserved hosts are not consumed merely by research.

An independently supplied 481-minute research requirement becomes **240.5 minutes**: sixteen full phases and one **30-second final phase**. A separately genuine progress loss leaving five minutes outstanding requires five minutes, not fifteen. Neither example grants a new recipe minimum or a progress-loss power.

Other research tasks retain their own actual rules. Teaching, ordinary formula copying, ritual learning, Scribing Insight’s distinct route, fixed waits and rest do not acquire these phases or discounts by association.

## 3. FT84-Q03 — eligible creation includes actual feat-granted construction

### Selected category interpretation

**A catalog recipe ID is not required when an actual feat already authorizes the physical creation process.** Craftsman’s printed benefit includes personally led eligible non-artisan creation.

A fixed printed duration is not, by itself, an exclusion. Explicit exclusions still control: Master Smithing’s temper and Combat Engineering’s kill-zone preparation remain unchanged.

### Contraption Crafter: five uninterrupted minutes

Its ten-minute base becomes **five uninterrupted active minutes** with an actually applicable Craftsman benefit.

Everything else remains:

- Actual Gnome heritage, usable tools, the same suitable **5 gp parts**, and the same **24-elapsed-hour use**.
- Parts and use committed at construction start; the prior gadget ends at that actual new start.
- Interruption forfeits the committed attempt, with no working gadget, saved partial work or completion roll.
- One actual d4 roll at completion; the same one-hour lifetime begins at actual completion.

The positive fixture completes at **300 seconds**, expires at **3,900**, and retains the next-use deadline **86,400**.

The interrupted branch stops at 240 seconds: parts/use remain spent and no gadget exists. Remaining parts do not permit an immediate retry. A genuine next-use attempt at 86,400 requires a fresh full five minutes and a fresh parts lot.

The supplied evidence names the worked **d4 = 3 clamp** outcome and the common Tiny/1 lb/AC10/HP1 body. It does not include the separately referenced complete four-profile activation table. **Construction is resolved here; unprovided clamp activation values are not invented or claimed tested.**

### Trapsetter: fifteen active minutes, without importing uninterrupted assembly

Its actual thirty-minute prepared-kit assembly becomes **fifteen active minutes**. The same parts, credential, tools, DC12 completion check and failure consumption remain.

**Unlike Contraption, Trapsetter does not say the assembly must be uninterrupted.** The new narrow work-credit completion therefore retains actual usable physical assembly work across pauses. A pause earns no work or protection; destroyed work or unusable parts cannot remain credited. An unfinished kit has no function.

The positive snare fixture uses actual cord and frame stock:

```text
d20 8 + INT 3 + PB 3 = 14 against DC 12
```

The failure reset totals 11, expends the actual cord and retains only the recoverable frame.

The pause case performs **seven minutes of work, pauses for one minute, then performs eight more minutes**. It completes at **16 elapsed minutes with 15 active minutes**—without importing Contraption’s forfeiture or advanced manufacturing’s stabilization.

Assembly does not spend or refresh quick-placement allowances, arm a trap, clear an existing slot, reset hard-control history or reduce later placement, disarming, collection and Reaction costs.

### Other source-qualified processes

| Process | Selected treatment |
|---|---|
| Bowyer’s authorized bow/arrow creation | Eligible through its actual bounded creation permission |
| Master Smithing’s authorized weapon/armor creation | Eligible; its separate temper is not |
| Combat Engineering barricade creation | **60→30 minutes**, not 15 from multiplying two half-factors |
| Master Smithing temper | **480 minutes unchanged** |
| Combat Engineering kill-zone preparation | **10 minutes unchanged** |
| Encoding, repair, collection, services and fixed waits | No Craftsman creation discount |
| Actual recipe121 manufacturing | **240→120 minutes**, retaining its own incorporation, phases, stock, station and zero-assistant limit |

FA13’s whole-job repair boundary also remains intact. A genuine authorized twenty-minute repair can receive its PB addition. Doing the last twenty minutes of an eight-hour job during rest does not qualify; charges, service and fuel remain spent.
